articles.content:
Hi HN, I’m building Codela to help coding agents learn from what happens after their code ships.I realized that my AI agent writes a change, the tests pass, and it gets deployed. Then in production a problem happens, I fix it, but what it did wrong and why never reaches the agent, so futures session usually make the same mistake.Codela checks every deploy against how your app actually behaves in production, learns from the ones that broke it, and teaches your agents so they don’t repeat the mistake.Would love any feedback on this, thanks!

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，据《连线》报道，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋早在承认婚外情之前一年，就已开始与一家擅长处理公众丑闻的危机公关公司合作。据两名知情人士透露，至少从 2025 年 10 月起，公关公司 Heller 就一直在幕后负责黄仁勋的相关公关事务。而就在今日，黄仁勋承认与一名女性存在婚外情。Heller 创始人丽莎 · 海勒（Risa Heller）在业内以处理权势人物的性不端指控及其他个人丑闻而闻名。根据《纽约杂志》2023 年的一篇人物报道，她曾为多位陷入争议的知名人士提供公关服务或咨询，包括美国前国会议员安东尼 · 韦纳（Anthony Weiner）、名厨马里奥 · 巴塔利（Mario Batali）以及作家杰弗里 · 图宾（Jeffrey Toobin）。当然，Heller 也为客户处理企业公关事务以及其他与个人争议无关的问题。据知情人士透露，外界最初认为，黄仁勋聘请这家公关公司的目的主要与个人生活有关，包括其家族的慈善事业。消息人士透露，Heller 团队经常与黄仁勋及其女儿麦迪逊 · 黄（Madison Huang）沟通。后者是英伟达产品营销总监，近年来在公司内部的影响力日益提升。目前尚不清楚，Heller 早期为黄氏家族提供的服务是否涉及黄仁勋的婚外情。据《纽约时报》报道，2024 年起，黄仁勋开始公开与一名自称艾丽丝 · 黄（Alice Huang）的女性同行。2025 年 10 月初，黄仁勋与艾丽丝之间的关系，被《纽约时报》一篇长篇报道披露。这篇报道在英伟达高层内部引发紧张气氛。据知情人士透露，黄仁勋对相关报道颇为不满。当月月底，英伟达内部公关团队便接到指示：凡是涉及黄仁勋的媒体问询，无论属于个人生活还是商业事务，都必须将 Heller 公关公司纳入沟通流程。IT之家早些时候报道，黄仁勋今日承认了自己的出轨行为，并向家人、公司员工、董事会及股东公开道歉。他在发给英伟达员工的一封电子邮件中写道：“我对妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我所做的一切都没有任何借口。我对此深感抱歉。”

articles.title: 欧洲力推本土制造电池，或使一辆电动汽车成本增加 2100 欧元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，当前，欧洲政策制定者希望汽车电池更多地在本土生产。然而由于欧洲制造的电池成本更高，增加的费用最终很可能由购车者承担。当地时间 7 日，据外媒 insideevs 报道，布鲁塞尔智库布鲁盖尔今年 9 月发表的一份报告提出，旨在保护欧洲现有汽车制造商的政策，可能最终让消费者和纳税人为此买单。如果规定汽车必须使用欧盟生产的电芯，每千瓦时的成本可能从 50 欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 372.3 元人民币）上涨至 85 欧元（现汇率约合 632.9 元人民币）。一辆配备 60kWh 电池的汽车，仅电池成本就可能增加 2,100 欧元（现汇率约合 15,637 元人民币）。如果再加上拟议中的低碳钢使用要求，成本还可能增加 200 欧元（现汇率约合 1,489 元人民币）。相比之下，简化车辆型式认证程序预计只能让车企每辆车节省 61 欧元（现汇率约合 454.2 元人民币）。数据显示，欧盟汽车产量较 2019 年下降 19%，2025 年新车销量也比 2019 年少了 220 万辆，而整个汽车产业仍提供约 1400 万个就业岗位。布鲁盖尔指出，欧洲汽车出口并未停止，电池及电动汽车工厂每季度仍吸引约 30 亿欧元（现汇率约合 223.38 亿元人民币）投资。报告担忧的是，欧洲正逐渐流失汽车技术、供应商和海外客户。今年的巴黎车展就体现了欧洲车企面临的竞争。中国品牌带来了出色的软件、科技配置丰富的豪华内饰和先进的充电技术，欧洲车企则更多地强调品牌历史和设计。宝马 iX3 和奔驰纯电 GLC 证明，欧洲车企仍有实力与中国品牌竞争，但仅凭消费者熟悉的车标，已不像过去那样容易卖车。报告还援引法国的一项研究发现，与能够享受购车补贴的车型相比，失去补贴资格的电动汽车销量下降了 60%，补贴对电动汽车的整体普及速度不言而喻。

articles.title: 美国知名风险投资家科斯拉看好 AI 重塑互联网：能让网站“有生命”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（9）日晚间报道，美国知名亿万富翁风险投资家维诺德 · 科斯拉认为，所有访客看到相同网页的时代即将过去。他最新投资的 AI 初创公司 Coframe 希望借助 AI 重塑互联网，为每位访客提供量身定制的网页。“AI 让高度个性化定制成为可能，整个世界都因此改变了。”Coframe 希望打造被其称为“有生命的互联网”的网络环境。公司最近完成 2,500 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1.67 亿元人民币）A 轮融资，由科斯拉创投和 Hanabi Capital 共同领投，累计融资 3,500 万美元（现汇率约合 2.34 亿元人民币），但未公布估值。维诺德 · 科斯拉（Vinod Khosla），图源：WikiMedia科斯拉创投早在种子轮就投资了 Coframe。科斯拉相信，借助 AI，为每位网站访客提供专属页面这一酝酿多年的构想终于有望成为现实。科斯拉认为，上网浏览变得越来越麻烦了。他拿亚马逊举例称，过去 15 年来，亚马逊的购物体验越来越差，因为平台更愿意向用户推销自己想卖的商品，而不是展示最符合用户需求的内容。“另一种办法是为每个页面单独编写代码，但成本实在太高，速度也太慢。为每位用户定制网页确实是个很好的主意。”Coframe 由 AI 研究员兼创业者乔希 · 佩恩于 2023 年创立。佩恩曾在斯坦福大学学习数学和计算机科学，还曾参与创办获得汤姆 · 布雷迪支持的体育娱乐初创公司 Autograph。佩恩在经营一家面向消费者的企业时，发现许多工作繁琐且耗费人力，由此萌生了创办 Coframe 的想法。ChatGPT 问世后，他意识到生成式 AI 或许就是解决办法。“网站都是静态的，建好之后，所有访客看到的内容都一样。以后每次想改进，都得花费大量精力。”佩恩希望 Coframe 做的不只是利用 AI 生成更好看的落地页，而是通过分析顾客的行为，准确了解究竟是什么促使他们点击网页、购买商品。“所有内容都是量身定制的。消费者能够获得更符合自身需求的体验，也能更清楚地了解企业经营什么业务、提供哪些商品和服务。”营销技术向来不是风险投资机构特别热衷的领域。佩恩认为，这个行业的市场格局日趋固化，少数几家老牌巨头占据主导地位。其余众多供应商则主要提供营销活动测试、精准投放和效果评估等方面的小幅改进工具。佩恩看好 AI 为营销技术行业带来第二春：“互联网将拥有自己的生命力。技术进步非常快，离实现这一愿景越来越近，我们希望参与推动这一变化。”

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，11 月 2 日，美团龙猫发布面向长程智能体任务的原生多模态模型 LongCat-2.5。随后来到今天（9 日），美团宣布该模型正式开源。该模型采用 MIT 协议，支持商用推理部署与二次训练，无需额外授权，是面向长程智能体任务的原生多模态模型。在复杂代码库开发、完整项目构建、Visual Coding 与专业办公场景中，端到端交付能力均有明显提升。模型总参数 1.6 万亿，每个 token 激活约 480 亿参数，支持一百万上下文。针对显存与带宽受限的国产算力芯片，团队在模型架构、芯片适配与部署策略上也进行了深度协同优化。根据介绍，LongCat-2.5 在 Visual Coding 上表现出色，支持创意设计、3D 等任务。这些能力提升来自视觉表征层的改造：模型将视觉信号表示为多层级离散 token，与文本一样由主干模型统一处理，而非外挂视觉模块。具体而言，模型对原生分辨率视觉特征做残差向量量化，逐级补足细节；视觉 token 可离线预计算并缓存，减少在线计算量，也让分布式训练负载更均衡；视觉码本与主干联合训练，视觉与文本共享同一套主干参数，在同一语义空间内协同完成视觉理解与代码生成。此外，LongCat-2.5 采用 W4A4 高效推理方案，将专家权重与激活同时量化到 4 bit，并通过原生 INT4 矩阵乘法单元执行计算。IT之家附上有关链接如下：模型开源：https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.5技术博客：https://longcat.ai/blog/longcat-2.5/API 平台：https://longcat.chat/platform/product

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，Rockstar Games 旗下《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）首次向玩家展示了游戏的主界面音乐。随着 PS5 版游戏预载在新西兰开放，玩家开始分享一段合成器风格的背景音乐。这段音乐会在 PS5 主屏幕上选中《GTA 6》时播放。新西兰玩家成为全球首批能够预载《GTA 6》的玩家，同时也率先听到了 PS5 主屏幕上将游戏光标停留在其图标上时播放的背景音乐。IT之家注意到，这段音乐采用了舒缓的合成器曲风，带有浓厚的 20 世纪 80 年代复古气息。这与此前《GTA 6》宣传素材中出现的音乐风格相吻合，包括游戏预告片以及 Extended Look（加长版预览视频）开头和结尾使用的配乐。据 RockstarINTEL 报道，在游戏预载正式开放之前，这段音乐就已经通过 Razed 首次曝光。Razed 是一名开发者，曾为《GTA 5》制作 NaturalVision 画质增强模组。当时，《GTA 6》的相关文件已经出现在 PlayStation 商店的后台系统中。不过，这是否意味着玩家进入《GTA 6》后，也会听到这段音乐？答案未必如此。这段音乐实际上是在 PS5 主屏幕上播放的，类似于电影海报搭配背景音乐的形式，属于主机系统界面的一部分，并不一定与游戏内部菜单使用的音乐相同。目前，《GTA 6》PS5 版预载正在按照不同地区陆续开放，玩家可以从当地时间 11 月 10 日零点开始下载。Xbox Series X|S 版则将在 11 月 10 日格林尼治标准时间（GMT）零点面向全球玩家开放预载。

articles.title: Waymo 自动驾驶车辆遇到校车“超车成性”，NHTSA 展开召回整改效果调查
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，据路透社报道，美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）今天（9 日）宣布，对谷歌母公司 Alphabet 旗下自动驾驶公司 Waymo 的 2895 辆汽车展开召回整改效果调查，原因是 Waymo 车辆在经过校车时屡次违反交通安全规定。此次调查主要针对 Waymo 去年年底推出的软件修复措施是否有效。此前，Waymo 曾宣布完成全部车辆的软件更新，但大多数违规事件发生在此之后，车辆仍会超越亮起闪烁红灯的校车。NHTSA 将重点调查 Waymo 在 2025 年 12 月召回中修复的问题：车辆遇到闪烁红灯或伸出停车警示牌的校车时，虽然会先减速或停车，却又继续行驶并超越校车。监管机构指出，大部分违规事件发生在 2025 年 11 月之后，而 Waymo 当时声称已完成所有受影响车辆的软件修复。调查将评估软件修复是否有效，并查明车辆更新后为何仍然违规。Waymo 还面临另一项调查。今年 1 月，一辆 Waymo 自动驾驶汽车在加州圣莫尼卡一所小学附近撞到一名儿童。去年 10 月，NHTSA 也曾对 Waymo 展开初步调查，起因是有报道称，旗下无人驾驶出租车在校车附近行驶时未遵守交通法规。得克萨斯州奥斯汀独立学区共记录了 19 起违规事件，其中一次，一辆无人驾驶汽车短暂停车后，在学生仍在过马路时继续行驶。佐治亚州亚特兰大的公立学校也记录了 6 起违规事件。去年 12 月，Waymo 宣布自愿召回 3000 多辆搭载第五代自动驾驶系统的汽车，并通过软件更新解决问题。Waymo 称，所有受影响车辆在 11 月中旬就完成了软件更新，以确保车辆按规定减速，并在需要停车时保持静止。

articles.title: 苹果 iOS 27.3 代码曝光 Siri“个人记忆系统”，可记录用户各类信息
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，根据代码研究人员 pdfu 分享的最新代码发现，苹果正在开发一套个人记忆系统，有望帮助 Siri 记住用户生活中的各种信息。根据相关发现，在苹果 iOS 27.3 测试版中，这套系统包含一个名为“记忆图谱”（Memory Graph）的组件，旨在整理用户的人际关系、常去地点、日常习惯、健康状况、锻炼情况，以及激励用户或阻碍用户实现目标的因素。IT之家注意到，系统还设计了名为“记忆原子”（Memory Atoms）的数据单元，用于记录事实、观点、意图和事件，并关联相关人物、地点、时间及话题等具体信息。据 pdfu 介绍，这套图谱通过两种处理机制收集信息。其中一种负责将结构化数据转化为洞察，例如读取用户个人联系人名片中的姓名字段。另一种则借助设备端 AI 模型或苹果私有云计算（Private Cloud Compute），从 Siri 对话、信息、照片和健康数据等来源提取信息。目前，代码中似乎只出现了其中一种由 AI 驱动的信息处理机制。pdfu 认为，这套机制旨在通过一组内置问题识别用户的动机、面临的障碍以及可利用的资源。系统内置了 60 个问题，其中包括询问哪些日常习惯可能影响用户获得充足睡眠。不过，从目前曝光的代码来看，这套系统仍处于未完成状态。例如，pdfu 指出，代码中尚未出现创建“记忆原子”的处理流程。在后续解释中，pdfu 还区分了记忆图谱与另一套独立的显式记忆存储系统。后者为苹果搜索系统中的记录预留了存储空间，但目前还没有任何程序负责向其中写入记录。据称，这两套系统都采用了苹果版本的 Kuzu 图数据库。苹果于 2025 年收购了 Kuzu，但今年早些时候收购消息曝光时，外界尚不清楚苹果打算如何利用这项技术。事实上，Siri 目前已经具备个人情境理解能力，可以从邮件、信息和照片等应用中查找与用户生活有关的信息。此次曝光的代码并未透露这套尚未完成的记忆系统何时正式上线，也没有说明苹果将如何让用户管理和控制自己的数据。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 9 日消息，据路透社报道，Meta 今天（9 日）宣布将在全球推广 AI 年龄估算技术，把 Instagram 上另外数百万名青少年用户纳入“青少年账户”保护范围，即使他们填写的出生日期显示自己是成年人也不例外。在出台此项措施之际，Meta 因旗下平台涉嫌伤害未成年用户而面临多起诉讼。“青少年账户”功能覆盖 Instagram、Facebook 和 Messenger，内置多项保护措施，可自动限制哪些人能够联系青少年用户、他们能看到什么内容，以及每天使用应用的时间。本月起，美国的家长将陆续收到 Instagram 通知，了解平台如何根据青少年的年龄采取相应保护措施。此外，Meta 还开始在澳大利亚利用苹果提供的用户年龄区间信息，辅助判断用户的实际年龄。这项技术也在向 Facebook 推广，Threads 则计划今年晚些时候开始在全球范围铺开。Meta 因旗下平台涉嫌伤害青少年而面临多起诉讼。今年 8 月，Meta 与美国几乎所有州和属地达成和解，协议总金额最高达 180 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,202.37 亿元人民币），以了结各地总检察长针对其平台伤害青少年问题提起的诉讼。根据和解协议，Meta 同意改进对青少年及 13 岁以下儿童的识别方式。上个月，Meta 还在洛杉矶的一起诉讼中与一名青少年原告达成和解。该案主要审理 Instagram 和 Facebook 是否因容易让用户上瘾的设计，导致青少年出现心理健康问题和饮食失调。

Abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) is challenging for social media data in a low-resource language. Abstract: Retail product catalogs assembled from web image search are cheap to build and pervasively noisy: queries return packaging shots instead of products, and entries proliferate under names that cannot be distinguished visually. Consolidating such a catalog can look like an alternative to scaling the model. We study a public archive of 165,769 cheese images across 1,824 query-named entries. Abstract: We fine-tune a pre-trained V-JEPA1 predictor from bidirectional latent inpainting to action-free causal forecasting while keeping the encoder frozen. Abstract: Fish stock assessments need fish lengths paired with species from far more places than trained surveyors can reach. Recreational divers already visit many of those places, but measuring a fish underwater has required trained observers or specialist equipment. Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on static visual understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to act in dynamic environments remains less well understood. articles.title: Federated training performs as well as centralized for 3D Latent Diffusion for Diagnosis-Conditioned Brain MRI Synthesis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.08771v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative models of brain MRI are useful to understand brain conditions, and to enrich scarce and imbalanced neuroimaging data. However, training these models requires large, multi-site training sets, which is challenging. Federated learning (FL) allows for training deep learning models without sharing data. We show that training a 3D conditional latent model federatedly (where data is kept private at each site) performs similarly to centralized training (where all the data have been copied to a single site). We evaluate three metrics: conditional fidelity (how well generated MRIs perform in classification), diversity (how the generated images match the real data distribution, using MultiScale-SSIM), and realism (how close generated images are to real images, using Fr\'{e}chet Inception Distance). Our results show that federated training is a viable route to develop multi-site generative models of brain MRI.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.08802v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent diffusion models rely on pretrained autoencoders that introduce lossy compression and constrain spatial granularity. Abstract: Partial occlusions challenge object recognition in both human and computer vision (CV), but the impact is largely dependent on the occlusion and model design. articles.title: The APL Doesn't Fall Far From The Tree: Unsupervised Artefact Prototype Learning in Histopathology
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.08838v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Histopathology foundation models provide rich representations of tissue morphology, but technical artefacts in whole slide images introduce noise that may impact diagnostic accuracy. We introduce Artefact Prototype Learning (APL), a novel approach to detecting these artefacts that exploits the geometry of pre-trained embedding spaces without manual labels or fine-tuning. Rather than treating artefacts as isolated outliers, APL computes prototypes of out-of-distribution patches and uses them to distinguish artefact-associated patterns from tissue. Evaluation on a single-centre dataset shows that APL outperforms prior methods GrandQC and HistoART in detecting artefacts such as blur, dark spots, slide edges and pen marks, but struggles with tissue folds and blood. These results show that frozen pre-trained embeddings already carry information that allows artefact detection without expensive labels or vast computational resources.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.08861v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Align3D, an image-conditioned diffusion model that generates 3D indoor layouts that are both faithful to a single input photograph and physically plausible beyond the observed view. From the photograph we infer a confidence-calibrated scene graph and train a set-diffusion layout denoiser with image-structure co-alignment where confidence-weighted modality fusion balances image and scene-graph alignment using predicted confidences, while observability-aware fidelity-preserving guidance projects conflicting scene-quality gradients and reweighs them with an object-level confidence mask so under-observed degrees of freedom absorb physical priors without undoing the image-graph match. On 3D-FRONT, Align3D improves image-alignment and scene-quality metrics over recent baselines; once trained, it maps previously unseen photographs to layouts in a single feed-forward pass.

Abstract: As robots are deployed in the real world, they will inevitably make mistakes. Abstract: A flow-matching policy deployed in the field must often satisfy a constraint that was absent from its demonstrations, such as avoiding an obstacle it has never seen. Abstract: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support. articles.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
articles.content: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

articles.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
articles.content: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation.

articles.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
articles.content: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.

articles.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
articles.content: Scenario-based simulation is central to evaluating autonomous-driving policies, but a scenario scripted before execution (i.e., with predetermined, fixed actor routes and speeds) may not preserve its intended interaction once the tested ego policy responds in closed loop. Scripted scenarios cannot adapt to unanticipated ego behavior, while learned traffic actors may remain reactive without reliably realizing a particular scenario intent. We introduce a scenario orchestrator that continuously monitors the joint traffic state and adapts non-ego actors through re-timing, re-routing, and role reassignment for creating a specific scenario intent. At each step, the orchestrator solves a constrained optimization problem that preserves the intended interaction while limiting interventions and maintaining traffic feasibility. We further distinguish scenario realization from policy failure, allowing a test to first be judged based on whether the intended interaction occurred and then by how the ego policy responded. Experiments in the CARLA simulator across multiple scenario families and driving policies show that orchestration realizes targeted interactions more reliably than scripted and learned actor-level baselines, particularly under variations in initial conditions and ego behavior. These results support closed-loop scenario orchestration as a tool for controlled and reproducible policy evaluation.

articles.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
articles.content: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

articles.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
articles.content: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. In contrast, we present a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents, modeling both global trajectories and root-relative poses. A B-spline reparameterization compresses the generative state space while enforcing temporal smoothness, and a dual-stream transformer conditions each agent's predictions on observed neighbor motion for interaction-aware forecasting. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on CMU-Mocap (UMPM) and 3DPW, outperforming deterministic baselines on joint position error, pose error, and final displacement error despite producing a full predictive distribution. We additionally establish the first motion prediction baseline on WorldPose, a large-scale professional soccer dataset, where social conditioning demonstrably concentrates predictive uncertainty along interaction-constrained directions.

articles.title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
articles.content: Zeolites are an important class of porous crystalline materials with broad applications in gas storage, separations, and catalysis. Although hundreds of thousands of experimentally realized and hypothetical zeolite structures are known, identifying materials optimized for a target application remains challenging because property labels are expensive to obtain and available only for limited structure-molecule pairs. While prior work has demonstrated that 3D neural representations can predict zeolite properties effectively, it remains unclear which representation-learning strategies are most effective in the low-data regime relevant to materials discovery. We present ZeoBench, a benchmark for self-supervised learning on dense 3D representations of all-silica zeolites, and evaluate the resulting features on six existing downstream adsorption-property prediction tasks, across a range of training set sizes. Our study compares self-supervised 3D pretraining on volumetric zeolite data, adaptations of image-pretrained 2D ConvNets and vision transformers to 3D via multiview and channel-inflation strategies, and 3D ConvNets pretrained on out-of-domain volumetric datasets, alongside hand-crafted descriptors and supervised baselines. Using our pretraining and evaluation framework, we find self-supervised 3D representations outperform existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance across both in-domain label regimes and for the unseen domain of metal organic frameworks. Learned representations consistently outperform hand-crafted descriptors, and convolutional architectures are generally more effective than vision transformers in this setting. These results establish ZeoBench as a practical benchmark for 3D representation learning in zeolites and provide guidance for data-limited adsorption property prediction.

articles.title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
articles.content: The Gaussian jet of an image is a graded vector space: a dilation by $λ$ multiplies derivatives of order $k$ by $λ^{-k}$. Local graded convolutions are exactly homogeneous differential operators, and a local feature is dilation-invariant if and only if it factors through the scale-normalized jet or, without the scale, through the retraction onto the weighted sphere of the grading. Under unknown Gaussian blur the retraction changes only by a change of scale, whereas the scale-normalized jet acquires a grading factor that no radial normalization removes. At the zero jet the retraction separates image families that radial normalizations and continuous classifiers cannot. Networks built on the retraction are universal for invariant features. On MNIST such a network keeps 88.4% accuracy under a two-pixel blur, against 66.2% for the same network on scale-normalized derivatives; in Lindeberg's Gaussian derivative network the retraction raises accuracy at that blur from 91.5% to 95.1%.

articles.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
articles.content: Tendon-driven continuum robots can reach through constrained spaces, but contact along their bodies is invisible to the sensors at their motors. We show that this is a structural limitation rather than a tuning problem: the map from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space of dimension at least seven, so no estimator that leaves the contact support free can locate contact. When the obstacle geometry is known, however, non-penetration and complementarity make the contact force locally identifiable, and we prove that the resulting system with unknown contact inputs is locally exponentially strongly detectable. We present a constrained moving horizon estimator (MHE) that encodes these conditions and runs in real time as one quadratic program per sample, and we give a local, mode-wise robust stability result for it. In a finite- element benchmark of a two-section robot pressing and sliding on a wall, the estimator located contact to 0.9 mm and estimated contact force to 0.22 N, compared with 65 mm and 0.72 N for a tuned extended Kalman filter (EKF) with state projection. The estimator tolerated millimeter- level errors in the obstacle position and unmodeled wall friction, under which the projected EKF failed. Under randomized model mismatch over 40 trials, including unmodeled tendon friction, it remained better in force and location in every trial. Without contact, the MHE offered no advantage over the EKF, which confirms that its benefit comes from the contact constraints. This report extends a letter submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters with complete proofs and additional experiments.

articles.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.

articles.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
articles.content: Large reasoning models (LRMs) improve task performance by generating longer intermediate reasoning traces, but this substantially increases inference costs and makes low-precision quantization increasingly important. However, aggressively quantized models often perform poorly on reasoning tasks. We observe larger activation fluctuations during the first decoding steps of reasoning. Calibration that omits these early states may miss their activation fluctuations. To address these reasoning-specific quantization challenges, we propose \textbf{CodeQuant2}, a clustering-based LUT quantization framework for low-precision large reasoning models. CodeQuant2 mitigates activation outliers with rotation and scaling, uses clustering to represent non-uniform weight distributions, and adapts codebook sizes to the quantization difficulty of each layer. Guided by our observation of reasoning-time activation behavior, CodeQuant2 further improves calibration sample selection to better match actual decoding statistics. Combined with our customized LUT CUDA kernel, CodeQuant2 delivers substantial accuracy improvements on reasoning benchmarks while achieving up to $2.85\times$ speedup over BF16.

articles.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
articles.content: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge.   Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation.   Results: On the EndoVis-18 benchmark, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.88, compared with 4.23 for SGT and 3.36 for the strongest conventional Transformer baseline. Exact instrument-action-target triplet-set accuracy reached 52.6%, compared with 32.7% for SGT and 26.2% for the strongest conventional baseline. These results demonstrate improvements in language quality and factual agreement. On TORS, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.06, compared with 3.80 for the strongest baseline.   Conclusion: GRAC demonstrates that combining structured surgical scene representations with retrieved examples improves surgical scene captioning and produces more contextually meaningful descriptions.

articles.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
articles.content: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations and distill the learned critic into a lightweight grasp utility network that ranks candidate grasps using only the candidate grasp configuration and goal information. At inference time, we select the grasp with the highest predicted downstream utility for the downstream policy to complete the task, before even making a contact. Experiments demonstrate that Grasp-TAGS improves rearrangement success over both fixed single-grasp policies and random grasp selection, achieving an average success rate of 89.84% compared with 79.87% for the best-performing single-grasp policies, an improvement of 9.97 percentage points. Grasp-TAGS also reduces final orientation errors across all evaluated objects. For more qualitative results, refer to the supplementary webpage: https://rpm-lab-umn.github.io/Grasp-TAGS-web-page/

articles.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
articles.content: Many multimodal alignment problems require mapping a source modality into a fixed space defined by a target modality, where the target space is not merely an intermediate embedding but is used directly for downstream analysis. In this setting, successful alignment should preserve both the global structure of the target distribution and the instance-level correspondence observed in paired source--target training data. Existing objectives typically address only part of this goal: contrastive losses encourage relative similarity, distribution-matching losses improve marginal agreement, and pointwise regression fits each source sample to its paired target without explicitly modeling target-space path geometry. We propose FlowAlign, a flow-guided target-space alignment method that repurposes conditional flow matching as a training-time alignment signal rather than an inference-time transport model. FlowAlign uses the learned flow field to guide the alignment of source-side representations with the fixed target space, encouraging them to preserve paired correspondence while remaining compatible with the global target-space structure. We further provide theoretical analysis showing how FlowAlign helps improve paired correspondence by controlling endpoint accuracy and capturing local target-space geometry. Experiments on synthetic data, paired single-cell multiome benchmarks, and image--text alignment demonstrate that FlowAlign improves instance level correspondence while preserving target-space structure across different modality settings.

articles.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
articles.content: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM and used it for the matching. Our question is whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Improving its accuracy required fusion with a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single shift per ground track, then per observation. For most tracks, the shifts nearly matched those from the airborne LiDAR DTM, likely because DTM errors canceled out across many observations. Per-observation corrections, however, did not match. At a single observation, the error does not cancel out and is too large for the correction. This error likely originates mainly from the input DTM. Therefore, even without a 1 m-resolution DTM, a roughly 10 m-resolution DTM, fused with a global DTM and super-resolved to 1 m, should yield track-wise corrections nearly matching those from a 1 m-resolution DTM.

articles.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
articles.content: The extent to which demographic-associated information is detectable across organs and disease states in routine clinical histopathology remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 1.3 million hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images from 257,322 patients across 25 organs, using pathology foundation-model representations and multiple-instance learning to systematically map information associated with sex, age group, and self-reported race. Across 69 organ-demographic combinations, demographic attributes were broadly recoverable, with pan-organ mean AUROCs of 0.828 for sex, 0.733 for age group, and 0.662 for self-reported race, and substantial variation across organs. Demographic-class balancing produced relatively small changes in performance, while evaluation within diagnosis-text clusters showed modest attenuation. Under training with diagnosis-based grouping, demographic-associated signals remained detectable across multiple organs, including sex in gastric tissue (AUROC 0.865), age group in breast (0.816), and self-reported race in skin (0.728). Literature-guided analysis of these settings generated candidate histomorphological and contextual explanations for further investigation. Together, these findings provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology, informing investigations of its sources, assessments of potential shortcut learning, and the development of more interpretable computational pathology models.

articles.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
articles.content: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1. The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. The hash-only sender delivered 857 of 1,000 messages on the first attempt and cost 192.8 bits per message, 18.4 bits more than PPM order 1 (95% bootstrap interval 10.9 to 26.3); by the pre-registered rule it spends more and is not equivalent within one byte. As secondary results we map measured sender memory against bits. The hash-only sender (8,190 B on a host build, keyed BLAKE2b tag included, as in every method) was the cheapest point in bits from 8,190 B up to, but excluding, PPM order 1 at 24,844 B, 45 to 46 bits below smaz2 and Unishox2; from PPM order 1 upwards, in-domain senders spend fewer bits, except order 2 pruned to 16 KiB. In airtime it loses to PPM order 1 on all five links priced, to Unishox2 on four, and to raw text with a tag on two, because each failure costs an acknowledgement frame and a fallback frame. A wider receiver search recovers half of the failures and makes the cost 7.7 bits lower than PPM order 1, at about three minutes of receiver time per failure, and still loses in airtime on four of five links. We report the measurement as a delimitation, with every deviation of the run.

articles.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
articles.content: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. These results suggest that the skills CUAs learn on software, such as visual grounding, precise clicking, and exploration, already carry over to embodied tasks, giving CUAs a far broader scope in embodied AI than previously realized. We therefore advocate that computer-use agents can be embodied generalists. Further, we advocate that, by following the training strategy that made computer-use agents general, embodied AI can converge on a single general model as well, ushering in a new era of general embodied AI. articles.title: AdaptivePnP: Fast Auto-Tuned Plug-and-Play for Deconvolution
articles.content: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods reconstruct images by alternating a data-fitting step with an image denoiser. Their performance depends on two parameters: the step size $γ$ and the measurement noise level $σ$. In practice, $γ$ is often tuned by grid search over validation images and must be retuned whenever the problem setting changes, and $σ$ is assumed known or estimated separately. We propose AdaptivePnP, a PnP framework that jointly estimates $σ$ and $γ$ at every iteration from the data-fitting residual. To do so, we apply the PnP virtual model to the data-fitting proximal map and show that the residual is zero-mean Gaussian with covariance parameterized by $γ$ and $σ$. However, when one parameter is much larger than the other, the residual carries little information about the smaller one and using the maximum likelihood (ML) estimator can degrade the PnP iterations. We therefore introduce the identifiable maximum likelihood (IML) estimator, which restricts the ML estimator to an identifiable window in which the normalized Cramér--Rao bound of every parameter is bounded by a user-specified tolerance. For the virtual model, this window is an interval of ratios $ρ= γ/σ$, so computing the IML estimate reduces to a one-dimensional search over $ρ$. We apply AdaptivePnP to two standard PnP methods, yielding algorithms that require neither a tuned $γ$ nor a known $σ$. On image deblurring and super-resolution, AdaptivePnP matches or outperforms PnP baselines tuned with the true $σ$. Code is available at https://github.com/hdubasullivan/AdaptivePnP.

articles.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
articles.content: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". The dataset PigAirwayPressure is not an outlier. Although the archive is the standard benchmark, whether its tasks resemble the problems TSC is meant to solve has rarely been examined. We find that several datasets are repurposed from their original task, built from toy setups, or have flawed test splits. We further question how representative the archive's ordered non-temporal sequences (e.g. spectra, shape outlines) are of real TSC, and the potential downsides from the decomposition of multivariate problems. Our findings call for more careful interpretation of archive-wide scores and greater attention to deployment-relevant evaluation. The audit is at https://github.com/automl/ucr-provenance-audit.

articles.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
articles.content: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. We describe a radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular tools to produce a structured report, and use it to measure what such a system can do with the tools from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices. Report generation is simulated on a large multi-modality report corpus, with the orchestrator given either a catalog of finding classes consolidated from the cleared devices, each available on the modalities it is cleared for, or an unlimited catalog in which any class can be requested, and planning either from the clinical indication or from the target report. Tool outputs are simulated from the reference report, so the comparison isolates tool availability and orchestration from tool error. With the cleared catalog and the indication alone, the orchestrator recovers under a third of the clinically actionable findings; recovery improves substantially with the unlimited catalog, and further when the plan is written from the target report. Attributing every missed finding to a cause shows that most are classes no cleared device offers for the study's modality, and that a third are classes or tools that were offered and not called. Adding the most frequently missing tools closes most of the gap to the unlimited catalog on held-out reports, whereas a smaller orchestrator with the unlimited catalog gives up the whole gain. Tool availability and effective orchestration are thus complementary constraints on comprehensive AI-assisted radiology reporting.

articles.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. To study how best to use monitors to mitigate reward hacking, we introduce and open source three realistic environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks: a coding environment hackable via test overwriting, a medical chat environment hackable via sycophancy, and a biography generation environment hackable via hallucination. We first focus on the coding environment, where we find that: (1) models can learn to evade highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic flaws in probes and LLM judges; (2) monitors that leak more learning signal during RL suppress reward hacking but are more often evaded; and (3) including easier problems in training can decrease reward hacking. We apply our findings to build better reward hacking monitors for the medical chat and biography generation environments that improve upon naive baselines to reduce reward hacking rates across seeds to before-training levels in some interventions. Our results demonstrate that our takeaways translate to new settings and that better monitor intervention designs are possible.

articles.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
articles.content: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at https://github.com/OpenBitSys/BitDecoding-FP4.

articles.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
articles.content: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.

articles.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
articles.content: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein representations and as a prior for editing them. Generation quality scales smoothly with depth and compute. As a lens, single GLP "meta-neurons" are the strongest probes of discrete Swiss-Prot concepts at both hosts, beating InterPLM's released SAE features, and lead on continuous properties at 8M though not at 650M; falsification tests show this is mostly concentration, not new information. As an editing prior, the on-manifold correction makes DiffMean steering of three biochemical properties effective and restores on-manifoldness, but only in isolation: re-embedding the sequences actually produced after several rounds of decoding, the structural plausibility is compromised. This is mainly reproduced in additional SAE-based clamping structural steering experiments, where only Helix motif succeeds. The naturalness failure is traced to the rewriting coverage and the decoder rather than the prior, highlighting what the method must clear before it can serve for both discovery-by-editing and discovery-by-exploration. Trained GLPs are released on huggingface.co/collections/HPAI-BSC/glprot.

articles.title: BEV3SR: Evidence-Aware 3D Spatial Reasoning from Video
articles.content: 3D spatial reasoning from video remains challenging for VLMs because videos provide sequential, view-local observations rather than persistent metric scene records. Many questions must be answered in a query-specified perspective rather than the observed camera viewpoint, and prompting with a fixed set of RGB views may miss sparse or occluded visual cues. To address these gaps, we introduce BEV3SR, a training-free and backbone-agnostic framework for RGB-D videos with camera parameters. BEV3SR turns video observations into queryable metric bird's-eye-view (BEV) scene memory and formalizes each query into an evidence-aware spatial task. The Spatial Task Formalizer specifies the query's reference frame, spatial constraints, objective, and evidence requirement. The evidence requirement determines the appropriate reasoning pathway. A query treated as requiring geometric evidence is handled by the Geometric Reasoner, which deterministically computes the answer using the metric BEV records in the query-specified reference frame. Otherwise, a query treated as requiring visual evidence is passed to the Visual Evidence Aligner, which uses BEV-indexed object records and their associated supporting views to retrieve object-consistent and scene-context RGB frames for VLM grounding. Within a standard 16-frame budget, BEV3SR consistently improves different VLM backbones across multiple 3D scene QA benchmarks, delivering large gains on spatially intensive questions and significant improvements on open-ended scene QA. These results demonstrate that BEV3SR offers an effective, efficient, and interpretable framework for explicit 3D spatial reasoning from video.

articles.title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
articles.content: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. Calibrating by forecast wind regime turns marginal coverage into regime-level coverage, cutting day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40% relative to pooled calibration while narrowing bands overall.
